one_liner: Sentry is a developer observability platform for monitoring application errors and performance, with a broad public REST API, an official hosted MCP server, and a published Composio toolkit.

auth.notes: Use OAuth2 for third-party integrations acting on behalf of users. Scoped internal-integration bearer tokens support single-organization automation, while some endpoints require a personal bearer token. API keys and Basic authentication refer to the same legacy mechanism, which is disabled for new accounts. DSN authentication works only on endpoints that explicitly support it.

access.notes: The cloud Developer account supports the documented team read and write tutorial. Creating an internal-integration token requires a Manager or Admin role in the developer's own organization. The pricing page lists API and third-party integrations under Team, so broader free-tier coverage is unverified. Self-hosted Sentry supports internal-integration tokens without a Sentry subscription fee, but developers must supply and operate the infrastructure. Public integration publication requires approval; development can begin in the creating organization before publication.

api.notes: The public v0 reference documents reads and writes across organizations, projects, teams, issues, and releases. A first toolkit could search issues, retrieve event details, and let users approve changes to issue status or assignment.

mcp.notes: The production HTTP endpoint uses OAuth and can be scoped to an organization or project. The official CLI provides a local stdio option, including for self-hosted Sentry. Experimental tools are optional.

verdict.rationale: Sentry documents listing and creating teams on a free Developer account, and internal integrations automatically install and generate a token for the creating organization. The public API also supports issue updates, and publication approval is not required to build a toolkit for the creating organization.

problems: The cloud pricing page (https://sentry.io/pricing/) places API and third-party integrations under Team, while the official API tutorial recommends a free Developer account. The tutorial supports basic free API use, but the exact free-tier endpoint and feature boundaries were not verified with live credentials.
The marketing MCP integration page did not load directly. The official MCP endpoint’s documentation and Sentry’s repository were readable and supplied the evidence instead.

verification.note: OAuth2 is explicitly supported for third-party applications acting on behalf of users. The quotes also support authentication tokens, legacy API keys via Basic auth, and DSN authentication. The note's claims about token scopes and which endpoints accept DSNs are not fully shown.

The API tutorial recommends a free Developer account for listing and creating teams, establishing a self-serve free path. The quotes also support free self-hosting with internal-integration tokens and show that publication approval is separate from development. The pricing-page claim in the note has no confirmed quote.

The public docs explicitly identify a REST API and describe resource management and issue updates. The note's specific claims about v0, event details, and issue assignment are not established by these quotes.

The Sentry-hosted site describes an MCP service, and the vendor's repository calls it a deployed production service. The precise /mcp URL and the note's CLI, scoping, and experimental-tool details are not established by the quotes.
The confirmed quote appears on Composio's Sentry toolkit page.

A free Developer account is recommended for an API tutorial that lists and creates teams; internal integrations generate tokens, and the public API supports issue updates. Publication approval does not prevent development in the creating organization, so buildable_now with no credential or API blocker follows.
